title: Multiple Defendants: Limited Admissibility of Evidence

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: I instructed you during the trial that certain evidence was admitted only against [a] certain defendant[s]. You must not consider that evidence against any other defendant.

bench_notes.text: The court has no sua sponte duty to give an instruction limiting evidence to one defendant; however, it must be given on request. (Evid. Code, § 355; *People v. Miranda* (1987) 44 Cal.3d 57, 83 [241 Cal.Rptr. 594, 744 P.2d 1127], disapproved of on other grounds in *People v. Marshall* (1990) 50 Cal.3d 907 [269 Cal.Rptr. 269, 790 P.2d 676].)

related_issues.text: See the Related Issues section to CALCRIM No. 303, *Limited Purpose Evidence in General*.
